abstract: Does human–AI collaboration necessarily heighten employees’ concerns for information privacy? Drawing on cognitive appraisal theory, this study challenges deterministic accounts of AI and privacy by proposing a dual-appraisal mechanism. Using a mixed-methods design (time-lagged survey and interviews), we show that human–AI collaboration simultaneously activates challenge and hindrance appraisals, producing divergent privacy responses. Challenge appraisals lead employees to interpret data practices as enabling performance and development, thereby reducing concern for information privacy. In contrast, hindrance appraisals frame AI as surveillance-oriented and autonomy-reducing, increasing privacy concerns. Importantly, AI intrusiveness weakens the challenge–privacy link while strengthening the hindrance–privacy pathway. Overall, the study develops a process-based model of workplace privacy, offering implications for responsible AI design and demonstrating that privacy concerns are cognitively constructed through appraisal dynamics rather than technological features.

ur.tldr: 基于认知评价理论，通过时滞问卷与访谈的混合方法，探讨人机协作对员工信息隐私关注的影响。研究发现协作同时激发挑战型与阻碍型双路径评价，产生相反效应：挑战型评价将数据实践视为绩效与发展的赋能因素，降低隐私担忧；阻碍型评价则将AI框定为监控与自主性威胁，升高隐私担忧。AI侵入性削弱前者、强化后者，揭示工作场所隐私关注是认知评价动态建构的产物。

title: Beyond the surveillance threat: when and how human-AI collaboration mitigates or magnifies employee privacy concerns
title_zh: 超越监控威胁：人机协作缓解或加剧员工隐私顾虑的时机与机制
